subject: [RFC 0/2] mm: add source selectors to memory.reclaim

reviews.author: Li Zhe
reviews.summary:
Li Zhe expressed concerns that the patch's approach using source selectors is not a replacement for implementing tiered memcg counters/limits, which would provide accounting and policy targets. He suggested that these directions are compatible and can be used together to improve kernel-driven behavior and user-space reclaim pressure.

Li Zhe noted that the proposed memory.reclaim algorithm does not address the underlying issues of reclaim, such as inverting the LRU and applying per-tier memcg limits, and instead aims to expose a source-scoped proactive reclaim actuator while keeping the kernel's reclaim policy in control. He expressed concern that this approach may be a 'hack' to avoid addressing these harder problems.

Reviewer Li Zhe pointed out that using `source=nodes` in memory.reclaim does not guarantee a one-shot net footprint change and instead requires a feedback loop of applying reclaim pressure, observing the new distribution, and iterating. They also disagreed with constraining zswap pool allocations based on source nodes.

Reviewer Li Zhe expressed concerns that the patch's reclaim interface may be a 'hack' to avoid addressing more fundamental issues in memory management, such as per-tier memcg counters and correct LRU handling. He suggested adding details to the cover letter demonstrating how per-node resident ratios work and requested clarification on what constitutes progress under different scenarios.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks for the detailed comments.

I agree that improving the default proactive/async reclaim behavior can
be useful, and I also agree that tiered memcg counters/limits would be
useful. I do not see source=nodes as a replacement for those directions.
They solve different parts of the problem: tiered counters/limits provide
accounting and policy targets, while source=nodes is only an actuator for
proactive reclaim.

So I think these directions are compatible. A better default reclaim
policy or tiered memcg limits can improve kernel-driven behavior, while
source=nodes gives userspace an explicit way to apply reclaim pressure
to a selected resident source.

---

That is fair, and I do not intend this to avoid improving reclaim or
adding better tier-aware memcg accounting. A better memory.reclaim
algorithm would also make source=nodes more useful, because source=nodes
still uses the existing reclaim path after selecting the resident source.
The goal here is narrower: expose a source-scoped proactive reclaim
actuator while keeping the kernel's reclaim policy in control. The old
nodes= discussion had ABI problems, but it also showed that a
nodemask-like source selector is a useful primitive for finer-grained
proactive reclaim control [1].

---

This is a good example of why source=nodes should not be described as a
one-shot net footprint guarantee. Assuming source=nodes:1, the request
applies reclaim pressure to memcg memory resident on node1. That may
free some space on node1 in the short term, which can provide room for a
later node0-to-node1 demotion step. If zswap allocation, kswapd, or memcg
reclaim later moves pressure back across tiers and node1 usage rises
again, that is part of the dynamic reclaim/tiering behavior.

So userspace cannot rely on one write to memory.reclaim to produce a
final per-node distribution. The intended usage is a feedback loop: the
controller observes the memcg's resident distribution, chooses the source
nodes it wants to relieve, applies source-scoped reclaim pressure,
observes the new distribution, and iterates.

I do not think this patch should make source=nodes constrain zswap pool
allocations. That would be a different and much stronger semantic. The
current intent is only to constrain the resident source from which memcg
reclaim applies pressure, while completion accounting remains the
existing memory.reclaim accounting.

---

Agreed. I will update the cover letter to make this model clearer. I
will also make clear that source=nodes is not a final net per-node
footprint guarantee and does not change memory.reclaim completion
accounting.

[1] https://lkml.org/lkml/2022/12/14/194

Thanks,
Zhe

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged that the patch needs to provide clear guarantees for userspace about what it can rely on, and expressed skepticism about the usefulness of feedback loop interfaces.

Author acknowledges need for additional testing and demonstration of the patch's reliability, specifically requesting tests to show the interface extension works as intended in various scenarios.
reviews.raw_body:
I think the critical question is what CAN userspace rely on?

We can make a bunch of feedback loop interfaces, but there's no
guarantee they'll actually be useful.

---

To be clear, I think not just making it clearer, but if you can show
some tests that demonstrate the reliable behavior of the interface
extension under different scenarios - that would be compelling.

~Gregory

2026-10-22.patch_summary: This patch proposes adding source selectors to memory.reclaim, which would allow for more granular control over memory reclaim policies. The goal is to enable per-tier resident ratio policies, where the system can prioritize reclaim from specific nodes or tiers based on their temperature (coldness). However, some concerns have been raised about the implementation approach, with suggestions that a more fundamental solution, such as tiered memcg counters, would be more effective and less prone to workarounds.
